title: Documentation
description: Complete OneSource guide: install, bundle, filter, configure and diagnose projects.

sections.title: What OneSource does
sections.html: OneSource bundles a local project into a directory tree and text file blocks for review or AI context. It supports glob filters, ignore rules, reusable profiles, clipboard output, dry-run previews and per-path diagnostics. Normal bundling stays local; installation and self-update contact GitHub.

sections.title: Suggested reading order
sections.html: If you are new, install first and complete Getting started. Then choose the topic by the problem you want to solve. Each topic provides its own starting files and steps; you do not need to finish the previous topic. CLI reference remains the place to look up exact types, defaults and command syntax.

sections.title: All documentation
sections.html:
• Installation — Get the correct executable onto PATH and verify it.
  • Getting started — Create a first bundle and inspect what you will share.
  • CLI reference — Look up an argument, alias, type or default quickly.
  • Filtering files — Include useful files and find why others are excluded.
  • Directory tree — Show a broad project map while attaching less content.
  • Configuration and profiles — Reuse settings and learn merge versus replacement.
  • Diagnose with explain — Diagnose a missing file, fix its rule and verify again.
  • Output and statistics — Choose a path or clipboard, then interpret counts and tokens.
  • Updating and source builds — Choose the update route appropriate to your installation.
  • Troubleshooting and limits — Work from an error to checks, correction and validation.

getting-started.title: Getting started
getting-started.description: Prepare a small project, preview selection, write your first bundle and inspect or copy its contents.

sections.title: Prepare a small project
sections.html:
Use this page when you want to produce your first bundle and check what you will share. You will preview three files, write a bundle, inspect it, then optionally copy it. A bundle is a text document containing a project tree and file contents; it does not compile or run the project.

In a new folder named demo, create the following files with a text editor. The text after each filename is its content; use a line break for each ↵. Use sample values only. Open a terminal in demo. Do not reuse a folder containing an existing .onesourcerc.

  • Cargo.toml: [package] ↵ name = "demo" ↵ version = "0.1.0" ↵ edition = "2021"
  • README.md: # Demo
  • src/main.rs: fn main() {}

OneSource must already be available as onesource. If it is not, follow Installation. All commands on this page start in this folder unless a step explicitly says otherwise.

sections.title: 1. Preview, then write the bundle
sections.html:
Run the preview first. --no-config uses built-in settings instead of loading a profile; --dry-run reads selected files and estimates the output without writing the bundle.

onesource --no-config --dry-run

Look for one [EXPECT] line for each prepared file and Files Processed: 3. The preview also prints the tree and planned output path. Token values vary with content and are not a pass/fail condition. No demo.onesource should exist yet.

[EXPECT] Cargo.toml (... content tokens)
[EXPECT] README.md (... content tokens)
[EXPECT] src/main.rs (... content tokens)
Files Processed: 3

Once the selection is correct, remove --dry-run. This is the step that creates the file; it uses the same selection rules as the preview.

onesource --no-config

Expect Output saved to: followed by the path to demo.onesource. Because your terminal is inside demo, the file is also inside demo. If you run from another working directory, the default output goes there instead.

sections.title: 2. Open and inspect the output
sections.html:
Open demo.onesource with a text editor. The tree gives orientation; each following <file path="…"> block contains the named file’s text. Check filenames and contents before sharing. Seeing a filename in the tree alone does not guarantee that its contents were attached.

demo/
├── Cargo.toml
├── README.md
└── src/
    └── main.rs
<file path="Cargo.toml">
[package]
...
</file>

<file path="src/main.rs">
fn main() {}
</file>

This is an excerpt: the actual bundle also contains the README block and full Cargo.toml. Terminal progress is not the complete bundle. [SKIP] during preview means a selected candidate could not be attached; inspect its reason before proceeding.

sections.title: 3. Select less content or copy the bundle
sections.html:
To share only the Rust source, add an include filter. -i "src/**" keeps paths under src; -o review.onesource gives the result a deliberate name. Preview that selection before writing it.

onesource --no-config -i "src/**" --dry-run

Expect only src/main.rs as an attached candidate, with Files Processed: 1. Now write it:

onesource --no-config -i "src/**" -o review.onesource

For a clipboard workflow, use the same selection with --copy. It sends the complete bundle to the desktop clipboard instead of creating an output file. Paste into a text editor first to inspect it; then paste into your intended destination.

onesource --no-config -i "src/**" --copy

Expect Output copied to clipboard successfully!. This step does not update review.onesource. If clipboard access fails in SSH or a headless session, use the file command above. Learn selection rules in Filtering and saved settings in Profiles.

cli.title: CLI reference
cli.description: Every OneSource argument, option, alias and command.

sections.title: Syntax and boolean values
sections.html:
onesource [PATH] [OPTIONS]
onesource [PATH] profile <COMMAND>
onesource [PATH] explain <PATHS>... [OPTIONS]
onesource update
onesource help profile update

Persistable boolean options and --show-arg accept a bare flag (true) or =true/=false; use --no-tree=false, not --no-tree false. Action flags such as --copy, --save and --dry-run do not accept =false. Top-level options are not global: put root and top-level options before the subcommand. Explain and profile create/update have their own options after the subcommand.

sections.title: All arguments and options
sections.html:
SyntaxField, type, defaultCommands and profile storageBehavior and example
[PATH]path
directory; .		Top level
Profile: no		Scan root; must exist and be a directory. Put before subcommands. Config is read only from PATH/.onesourcerc; no ancestor search.

onesource ./my-project --dry-run

Preview the given root.

-o, --output-path PATHoutput_path
path; <root-name>.onesource		Normal + explain + profile create/update
Profile: yes		Relative to the working directory, even with another scan root. Current output is always excluded. Parent must already exist for file output.

onesource -o review.txt

Write review.txt in the working directory.

-i, --include GLOBSinclude
string; unset (all)		Normal + explain + profile create/update
Profile: yes		Comma-separated patterns. Empty string clears the filter; blacklist and ignore still apply. Tree inherits unless overridden.

onesource -i "*.rs" --dry-run

Preview eligible Rust files.

-x, --exclude GLOBSexclude
string; unset		Normal + explain + profile create/update
Profile: yes		Exclude wins over include. Empty string clears this filter. Tree inherits unless overridden.

onesource -x "*.log" --dry-run

Remove log paths from content and inherited tree.

--tree-include, --ti GLOBStree_include
string; inherit include		Normal + explain + profile create/update
Profile: yes		Overrides only the tree include; use ="" to show all otherwise eligible tree paths.

onesource -i "*.rs" --ti "*.toml" --dry-run

Tree shows TOML; content selects Rust.

--tree-exclude, --tx GLOBStree_exclude
string; inherit exclude		Normal + explain + profile create/update
Profile: yes		Overrides only the tree exclude; empty string removes inherited exclusions.

onesource -x "*.log" --tx "" --dry-run

Tree no longer inherits log exclusion.

--no-ignore[=BOOL]no_ignore
boolean; false		Normal + explain + profile create/update
Profile: yes		Disables standard ignore filters for content. Tree inherits unless tree-no-ignore is set. Does not disable blacklist.

onesource --no-ignore --dry-run

Ignore rules bypassed, blacklist retained.

--tree-no-ignore[=BOOL]tree_no_ignore
boolean; inherit no_ignore		Normal + explain + profile create/update
Profile: yes		Independent ignore override for tree. Explicit false keeps tree ignore rules even with --no-ignore.

onesource --no-ignore --tree-no-ignore=false --dry-run

Tree still honors ignore.

--no-tree[=BOOL]no_tree
boolean; false		Normal + explain + profile create/update
Profile: yes		Omits the tree only; file content is unaffected.

onesource --no-tree --dry-run

No tree, file preview remains.

--no-blacklist[=BOOL]no_blacklist
boolean; false		Normal + explain + profile create/update
Profile: yes		Disables built-in blacklist for both content and tree. Current output still excluded; ignore and glob filters remain.

onesource explain .env --no-blacklist

No built-in blacklist block for .env.

-m, --max-size KIBmax_size
nonnegative usize; 500 KiB		Normal + explain + profile create/update
Profile: yes		Content only. Rejects bytes > KIB × 1024; equality is allowed. Zero admits only empty files. Tree unaffected.

onesource -m 1 --dry-run

At most 1024 bytes per content file.

--desc TEXTdescription
string; unset		Normal + explain + profile create/update
Profile: yes		Stored with --save or profile create/update. Does not change selection. Empty string is allowed. Explain accepts but ignores it.

onesource --desc "Review" --save --dry-run

Store description in default.

-p, --profile NAMEprofile
string; default		Normal + explain
Profile: no		Loads exactly one profile, without merging default into named profiles. Missing explicit profile is an error unless --no-config.

onesource -p review --dry-run

Preview with an existing review profile.

--no-configno_config
flag; false		Normal + explain
Profile: no		Skips loading config; --save still reads and writes the config document.

onesource --no-config --dry-run

Use built-in values and explicit CLI options.

--dry-rundry_run
flag; false		Normal + explain
Profile: no		Reads files and estimates output without writing bundle or clipboard. --save still persists config before scan.

onesource --dry-run

Print expectations and estimates; no bundle.

-c, --copycopy
flag; false		Normal + explain
Profile: no		Copies entire bundle instead of writing file. --dry-run suppresses copy. Clipboard failures stop execution.

onesource --copy

Copy bundle; no output file.

--savesave
flag; false		Normal + explain
Profile: no		Upserts explicit persistable options into active profile before scan; a later scan failure does not undo save.

onesource -i "*.rs" --save --dry-run

Merge explicit include into default.

--replacereplace
flag; false		Normal + explain
Profile: no		Requires --save in normal runs; discards unspecified saved fields. profile update also supports --replace.

onesource --save --replace -i "*.rs" --dry-run

Stored default contains only explicit include.

--show-arg[=BOOL]show_arg
boolean; false		Normal + explain
Profile: no		Prints resolved AppConfig after normal execution and statistics. Explain accepts but does not print it.

onesource --show-arg --dry-run

Print resolved arguments after statistics.

-h, --helphelp
flag; no execution		All commands
Profile: no		Shows help for the current command. help subcommand is also available. Not a setting.

onesource explain --help

Show diagnostic command help.

-V, --versionversion
flag; no execution		Top level
Profile: no		Shows executable version at top level; not a setting.

onesource --version

Print installed version and exit.

sections.title: Overrides and help
sections.html:
onesource --no-config --no-tree=false -m 1 --dry-run
onesource --include="" --tree-exclude="" --dry-run
onesource explain src/main.rs --no-ignore=false
onesource profile --help
onesource profile update --help
onesource explain --help
onesource --version

The first preview allows content up to 1024 bytes and keeps the tree. Empty filters override saved strings. For each option, the behavior column describes its interactions; use the corresponding detailed page for output examples.

filtering.title: Filtering files
filtering.description: Learn include and exclude step by step, choose glob patterns, and resolve ignore or blacklist exclusions.

sections.title: Decide what belongs in a bundle
sections.html:
Use filters when a project contains more than the recipient needs. In this walkthrough you will include Rust files, remove legacy code, then investigate an ignored note. Include defines the allowed set; exclude removes paths from that set. Neither one overrides ignore rules or the built-in blacklist.

In a new folder named demo, create the following files with a text editor. The text after each filename is its content; use a line break for each ↵. Use sample values only. Open a terminal in demo. Do not reuse a folder containing an existing .onesourcerc.

  • README.md: # Demo
  • src/main.rs: fn main() {}
  • src/util.rs: pub fn value() -> u8 { 1 }
  • src/legacy/old.rs: fn old() {}
  • tests/smoke.rs: #[test] ↵ fn smoke() {}
  • .gitignore: notes.txt
  • notes.txt: Local notes
  • .env: EXAMPLE_KEY=demo-only

OneSource must already be available as onesource. If it is not, follow Installation. All commands on this page start in this folder unless a step explicitly says otherwise.

sections.title: 1. Include the files you need
sections.html:
Start with the extension. -i is short for --include; quote the pattern so your shell does not expand it before OneSource receives it.

onesource --no-config -i "*.rs" --dry-run

The four expected content paths are src/main.rs, src/util.rs, src/legacy/old.rs and tests/smoke.rs. README.md is outside the allowed set. If your goal is application source only, narrow by directory instead:

onesource --no-config -i "src/**" --dry-run

Now expect the three files under src, with no tests/smoke.rs. To add the README as well, join patterns with a comma; matching either pattern is enough:

onesource --no-config -i "src/**,README.md" --dry-run

Expect the three source files plus README.md. A comma list is a union, not a sequence of filters.

sections.title: 2. Remove an unwanted subset
sections.html:
Keep the include from the previous step and add -x (short for --exclude). A trailing slash means the directory’s descendants.

onesource --no-config -i "src/**,README.md" -x "src/legacy/" --dry-run

Expect README.md, src/main.rs and src/util.rs: Files Processed: 3. old.rs matches include, but exclude wins. The tree inherits these filters, so legacy should disappear from it too. Once verified, write exactly that selection:

onesource --no-config -i "src/**,README.md" -x "src/legacy/" -o review.onesource

Open review.onesource and confirm three file blocks. If you want excluded content to remain visible as structure, use the independent tree controls.

sections.title: Learn to choose a glob pattern
sections.html:
A glob describes paths, not file contents. Use src/** for a subtree, *.rs for an extension, and an exact relative path for one file. ? matches one character; [ab] matches a listed character. For example, src/[mu]*.rs selects main.rs and util.rs in this fixture. Test patterns against actual paths rather than guessing.

onesource --no-config -i "src/[mu]*.rs" --dry-run

Expect two content files. To stop restricting include altogether, pass an explicit empty string:

onesource --no-config --include="" --dry-run

Expect README plus the four Rust files; notes remains ignored and .env remains blacklisted. An empty include means no include restriction, not an empty result. This also overrides a saved include when config loading is enabled.

Quote patterns to prevent shell expansion. Patterns are comma-separated, trimmed and backslashes are normalized to /. Empty entries are ignored; an empty list disables that filter. Globset supports *, ?, **, character classes and braces (avoid commas inside braces because the CLI splits commas first). Matching is case-sensitive. * may match across separators with the current default Glob settings. A trailing src/ becomes src/**. A simple name with no slash, star or dot, such as vendor, matches that name and descendants at any depth; names containing dots do not get this expansion. Invalid globs return an error.

sections.title: 3. Find out why include did not restore a file
sections.html:
Try asking for notes.txt explicitly:

onesource --no-config -i "notes.txt" --dry-run

Expect zero processed files because .gitignore excludes notes.txt before it can be selected. Ask explain for the reason:

onesource explain notes.txt --no-config -i "notes.txt"
Content:
  Result: blocked by ignore filters
Tree:
  Result: blocked by ignore filters

This is a report excerpt. --no-ignore disables the walker’s ignore rules; it does not remove the blacklist. If including the note is intentional, verify the change:

onesource --no-config -i "notes.txt" --no-ignore --dry-run

Expect notes.txt and Files Processed: 1. If the result instead says blocked by blacklist or exclude, changing ignore alone cannot help. Resolve the reported rule first.

Current output is excluded independently. Standard walker filters honor .ignore, .gitignore, Git exclude/global and parent ignore rules, even outside a Git repository; hidden files are not automatically excluded. Blacklist wins over user globs; exclude wins over include. An include cannot restore an ignored or blacklisted path. Explain reports blacklist before ignore, then exclude, then include; content then checks file type, size, NUL bytes and readability. --no-ignore disables standard ignore filters; --no-blacklist is separate.

sections.title: Understand and inspect the built-in blacklist
sections.html:
The blacklist protects common secret files, generated output and tool directories without needing project ignore rules. In this fixture .env holds a dummy value. Even with --no-ignore, it is still blocked:

onesource explain .env --no-config --no-ignore

Expect blocked by blacklist with Rule: blacklist = .env. To inspect a deliberately allowed sample, disable this separate layer:

onesource explain .env --no-config --no-ignore --no-blacklist

Expect included for both sections. This only diagnoses the sample and does not create a bundle. Do not carry --no-blacklist into a shared bundle without reviewing every selected path. The complete list follows:

Component names match case-insensitively anywhere in the path. Patterns match case-insensitively against the normalized path or filename. Disabling this list can include secrets and previous bundles; review the preview before sharing.

.git, .gitignore, .env, .onesourcerc, .svn, .hg, node_modules,
__pycache__, venv, .venv, .pytest_cache, .tox, target, .idea, .vscode,
.DS_Store, .npmrc, .pypirc, .netrc, id_rsa, id_dsa, id_ecdsa, id_ed25519

.env.*, credentials.json, service-account*.json, *.pem, *.key,
*.p12, *.pfx, *.onesource, .onesource-tmp-*, .onesource-backup-*

tree.title: Directory tree
tree.description: Show a project map independently from attached content, with before-and-after tree examples.

sections.title: Show context without attaching every file
sections.html:
Use a separate tree filter when the recipient needs a project map but only a small amount of source content. This page starts with the following independent fixture:

In a new folder named demo, create the following files with a text editor. The text after each filename is its content; use a line break for each ↵. Use sample values only. Open a terminal in demo. Do not reuse a folder containing an existing .onesourcerc.

  • README.md: # Demo
  • src/main.rs: fn main() {}
  • src/legacy/old.rs: fn old() {}
  • tests/smoke.rs: #[test] ↵ fn smoke() {}
  • .gitignore: notes.txt
  • notes.txt: Local notes

OneSource must already be available as onesource. If it is not, follow Installation. All commands on this page start in this folder unless a step explicitly says otherwise.

sections.title: 1. Observe default inheritance
sections.html:
Select only src/main.rs. With no tree-specific options, the tree inherits the content include:

onesource --no-config -i "src/main.rs" --dry-run
demo/
└── src/
    └── main.rs

Expect one content file. The src directory is added as an ancestor even though the include names a file. README, tests and legacy do not appear. Now override the tree include with an empty string:

onesource --no-config -i "src/main.rs" --tree-include="" --dry-run
demo/
├── README.md
├── src/
│   ├── legacy/
│   │   └── old.rs
│   └── main.rs
└── tests/
    └── smoke.rs

The tree expands, but the expected content remains only src/main.rs. --tree-include changes tree selection, not content. Its alias is --ti. The empty string means no tree include restriction; it still honors ignore and blacklist.

Tree include/exclude fall back individually to content include/exclude. An explicit empty string is an override that disables that tree filter. tree_no_ignore falls back to resolved no_ignore; explicit false overrides inherited true. no_blacklist affects both; no_tree disables tree generation entirely.

sections.title: 2. Override excludes and ignore separately
sections.html:
Suppose you want all Rust content except legacy code, while still showing that legacy directory in the project map. Content exclude normally propagates to tree; override it independently:

onesource --no-config -i "*.rs" -x "src/legacy/" --ti "" --tx "" --dry-run

Expect main.rs and tests/smoke.rs as content. The expanded tree still contains legacy/old.rs. --tx "" cancels the inherited exclude; to hide tests from the map instead, use --tx "tests/". It replaces the tree’s inherited exclude rather than adding to it.

For ignore rules, try including notes in content but keeping it out of the tree:

onesource --no-config --no-ignore --tree-no-ignore=false --dry-run

Expect notes.txt as content, absent from the tree. no-ignore is true for content, but the explicit false restores the tree’s ignore behavior. Use --no-tree when no map is needed:

onesource --no-config -i "src/main.rs" --no-tree --dry-run

Expect a file preview and statistics without any tree. no-tree does not disable attached content.

sections.title: 3. Verify tree and content as separate results
sections.html:
Write a small bundle that has a broad map but only one file’s content:

onesource --no-config -i "src/main.rs" --ti "" -o map.onesource

Open map.onesource. Compare tree entries with file-block paths: only src/main.rs should have a block. Do not infer attachment from the map. If a tree entry has no content unexpectedly, diagnose that path:

onesource explain README.md --no-config -i "src/main.rs" --ti ""
Content:
  Result: not included by include
  Rule: include = src/main.rs
Tree:
  Result: included

The excerpt explains the intentional difference: README matches the tree but not content. Size and binary detection can produce the same visible difference for another reason. Read Content first, then Tree.

The tree is sorted by name and inserts ancestors of matching paths. It does not inspect size, NUL bytes or content readability: a binary or oversized file may appear in the tree without a file block. Symlink directories are not recursively followed. A symlink outside root may appear in the tree but its content is skipped. Content candidates are sorted by relative path.

profiles.title: Configuration and profiles
profiles.description: Create and reuse profiles, try temporary overrides, and compare saved merges with replacement.

sections.title: Save a repeatable selection
sections.html:
A profile is a named set of bundling options, not a copy of project files. Use it when you repeatedly share the same subset. This walkthrough creates a review profile, applies a temporary override, edits saved settings, and compares merging with replacement.

In a new folder named demo, create the following files with a text editor. The text after each filename is its content; use a line break for each ↵. Use sample values only. Open a terminal in demo. Do not reuse a folder containing an existing .onesourcerc.

  • README.md: # Demo
  • src/main.rs: fn main() {}
  • tests/smoke.rs: #[test] ↵ fn smoke() {}

OneSource must already be available as onesource. If it is not, follow Installation. All commands on this page start in this folder unless a step explicitly says otherwise.

The folder must start without .onesourcerc. Only this page’s profile steps create it. Profile commands manage configuration; they do not create a bundle.

sections.title: 1. Create, inspect and apply a profile
sections.html:
Create review with source-only content and a size limit. The name follows create; the options that follow it are the settings to store. --desc helps you recognize its purpose later.

onesource profile create review -i "src/**" -m 100 --desc "Source review"

Expect Created profile. The command creates demo/.onesourcerc and no bundle. To inspect precisely what was stored, request JSON:

onesource profile show review --json
{
  "description": "Source review",
  "include": "src/**",
  "max_size": 100
}

No output_path or no_tree was stored because you did not specify them. --json requests machine-readable output; without it, show groups settings and labels absent fields as unset. List names and descriptions when you need to choose a profile:

onesource profile list

Expect review with its description. Apply it to a preview using -p, the short form of --profile:

onesource -p review --dry-run

Expect only src/main.rs as content. The 100 KiB limit and source filter come from review; dry-run applies only to this execution. To write that selection, use onesource -p review. A named profile does not inherit a profile called default.

sections.title: 2. Override for one execution without saving
sections.html:
You may need tests as well for one review. A CLI include replaces the saved include for this run; it does not add to it:

onesource -p review -i "src/**,tests/**" --dry-run

Expect src/main.rs and tests/smoke.rs, while max-size remains 100. Check the saved profile again:

onesource profile show review --json

It still says "include": "src/**". This is how you experiment without changing future runs. To ignore configuration altogether, use --no-config; it skips loading even if -p was supplied. An explicit --include="" removes the include restriction for a run, and --no-tree=false overrides a saved true boolean.

sections.title: 3. Update settings or save a tested command
sections.html:
To change a profile without bundling, use update. Only specified fields change; this is a merge:

onesource profile update review -x "tests/" --no-tree

Show review again. It should retain description, include and max_size, while adding exclude and no_tree:

{
  "description": "Source review",
  "include": "src/**",
  "exclude": "tests/",
  "no_tree": true,
  "max_size": 100
}

Alternatively, after testing a command you can save its explicit settings into the active profile. Here, make README part of future reviews and turn the tree back on:

onesource -p review -i "src/**,README.md" --no-tree=false --save --dry-run

Expect a Saved profile message, a tree, and README.md plus src/main.rs as content. show review should now have include="src/**,README.md" and no_tree=false; the existing exclude and max_size remain. Only explicitly supplied persistable options are saved, not dry-run or -p. Dry-run does not prevent configuration writes when --save is present. Save happens before scanning, so a scan failure does not undo it.

To establish defaults for runs without -p, save to the implicit default profile:

onesource --no-config -i "src/**" --save --dry-run

This creates or merges default. It does not alter review. For a new named profile, prefer create; --no-config -p NAME --save also allows creation, while requesting a missing named profile with loading enabled fails before saving.

sections.title: 4. Replace instead of merging
sections.html:
Use replacement when the old fields should be removed. Start from the profile edited above, then replace it with only a README include:

onesource profile update review --replace -i "README.md"
onesource profile show review --json
{
  "include": "README.md"
}

Description, exclude, no_tree and max_size are gone. Unset values now resolve to defaults, so the limit is back to 500 KiB and the tree is enabled. Run onesource -p review --dry-run to verify README alone is attached.

Normal bundling also supports --save --replace. To replace review without loading old fields into this run, use:

onesource --no-config -p review --save --replace -i "src/**" --dry-run

Expect the stored profile to contain only include="src/**" and the preview to process main.rs. Without --no-config, the current run may still use loaded old fields even though replacement removes them from disk. --replace requires --save in normal runs; profile update --replace does not.

sections.title: 5. Rename, describe or remove a profile
sections.html:
Give review a clearer name after the replacement step:

onesource profile rename review backend

list should now show backend, not review. To give it a new description without changing selection:

onesource profile update backend --desc "Backend source"

show backend should contain include plus description. Once the profile is no longer needed, delete it:

onesource profile delete backend

list no longer includes backend. Deleting a profile removes settings, not source files or bundles. Deleting default makes unnamed runs return to built-in settings. create fails on duplicate names; rename fails if the destination exists; show/update/delete fail when their named profile is missing. Names must be nonempty ASCII letters/digits, dots, underscores or hyphens.

sections.title: Understand the saved JSON and precedence
sections.html:
Open .onesourcerc in a text editor only after checking the saved profile. The top-level profiles object maps names to option objects. JSON uses underscores (output_path); CLI uses hyphens (--output-path). The description field corresponds to --desc. To configure by hand, save valid JSON and verify it with profile show before bundling. Here is a complete field example, separate from the walkthrough’s evolving profile:

JSON lives at scan-root/.onesourcerc. Explicit CLI values win over the selected profile, then built-in defaults apply. The default profile is optional; named profiles do not inherit it. Unknown fields are ignored by serde. Omitted or null fields use defaults/inheritance; empty strings and false are explicit values. Field types, defaults and effects are listed in CLI reference. Only the fields below are persisted; path, profile choice, copy, dry_run, save, replace, no_config and show_arg are not persisted.

{
  "profiles": {
    "default": {
      "description": "Source review",
      "output_path": "review.onesource",
      "include": "src/**",
      "exclude": "src/legacy/",
      "tree_include": "",
      "tree_exclude": "target/",
      "max_size": 500,
      "no_ignore": false,
      "tree_no_ignore": false,
      "no_tree": false,
      "no_blacklist": false
    }
  }
}

A supplied CLI value wins over the chosen profile, then built-in defaults apply. default is used only when no -p is provided, not as an inheritance base. Configuration is read from the scan root; to manage another folder use onesource /path/to/project profile list. Management commands still read configuration even with a top-level --no-config. Avoid concurrent manual edits: configuration writes are direct, not atomic.

sections.title: Legacy aliases and recovery
sections.html:
For existing scripts, profile ls is an alias for list and profile rm NAME is an alias for delete. The hidden legacy description command requires -p:

onesource profile desc "Backend source" -p default

This requires an existing default profile and merges its description; new scripts should use profile update default --desc "Backend source". list/show support the boolean flag --json (default false). create/update accept the persistable options from CLI reference; update --replace is a boolean action flag, default false. Each subcommand has --help.

If configuration is malformed or uses a flat old format, back it up and follow configuration migration. --no-config bypasses normal loading but does not bypass the config read required for --save. To clear an include without deleting the field use --include=""; to remove fields entirely, replace the profile or edit JSON.

explain.title: Diagnose with explain
explain.description: Diagnose missing files, interpret Content, Tree and Rule, correct the cause and preview again.

sections.title: Start with a missing expected file
sections.html:
Use explain when a preview or bundle is missing a file and you want the reason, rather than trying unrelated flags. It reports Content and Tree decisions for each requested path and does not create a bundle. Start with this independent fixture:

In a new folder named demo, create the following files with a text editor. The text after each filename is its content; use a line break for each ↵. Use sample values only. Open a terminal in demo. Do not reuse a folder containing an existing .onesourcerc.

  • README.md: # Demo
  • src/main.rs: fn main() {}
  • .gitignore: notes.txt
  • notes.txt: Local notes
  • .env: EXAMPLE_KEY=demo-only

OneSource must already be available as onesource. If it is not, follow Installation. All commands on this page start in this folder unless a step explicitly says otherwise.

sections.title: 1. Ask about the exact path and settings
sections.html:
Preview a note that .gitignore hides:

onesource --no-config -i "notes.txt" --dry-run

Expect zero processed files. Diagnose with the same include and no-config settings; place the target after explain:

onesource explain notes.txt --no-config -i "notes.txt"
════════════════════════════════════════
Path 1/1: notes.txt
  Content:
    Result: blocked by ignore filters
  Tree:
    Result: blocked by ignore filters
════════════════════════════════════════

Content answers whether text would be attached. Tree answers whether the path is selected for the map. Both are blocked here. There is no Rule line for ignore because this diagnostic reports the ignore layer, not the exact .gitignore line.

For another root, put it before explain; relative targets are interpreted inside that root:

onesource /path/to/project explain src/main.rs --no-config

Replace the example root with an actual folder. Multiple targets can be listed after explain; use the same active profile/options as the run you are investigating. For a saved review profile, use onesource explain src/main.rs -p review, provided that profile exists.

sections.title: 2. Change the relevant rule, then preview again
sections.html:
The reported reason is ignore, so changing include or tree-include will not solve it. If the note should normally remain ignored, bypass ignore only for this intentional selection:

onesource explain notes.txt --no-config -i "notes.txt" --no-ignore

Expect included for both sections. Now verify the entire selection, not just one path:

onesource --no-config -i "notes.txt" --no-ignore --dry-run

Expect notes.txt and Files Processed: 1. If the note should be included in every normal run instead, deliberately change your ignore rule and rerun the original preview. explain does not edit ignore files or configuration.

sections.title: 3. Read a matching Rule and separate tree from content
sections.html:
A file can be intentionally visible in the map without its text being attached. Ask about README with different content/tree includes:

onesource explain README.md --no-config -i "*.rs" --ti "*.md"
════════════════════════════════════════
Path 1/1: README.md
  Content:
    Result: not included by include
    Rule: include = *.rs
  Tree:
    Result: included
════════════════════════════════════════

The Rule tells you which include failed: *.rs does not match README.md. To attach README as well, replace the content include with a comma union:

onesource explain README.md --no-config -i "*.rs,README.md" --ti "*.md"

Expect included in both sections. Then validate and write:

onesource --no-config -i "*.rs,README.md" --ti "*.md" --dry-run

Expect README and main.rs as content, while the tree shows README only. To attach all content paths to the map too, remove the separate --ti override. For blacklist, use onesource explain .env --no-config: Rule identifies .env, so include cannot restore it. Keep real secrets excluded.

sections.title: What each result means and what to do next
sections.html:
Read the result before changing flags. The table maps every diagnostic string to a cause and an appropriate next check. A blocked result is still a successful diagnosis; it is not necessarily an execution error.

ResultCause and next action
includedThe path passes this section’s checks; verify the whole selection with dry-run.
included with lossy UTF-8 replacement charactersNon-UTF-8 text was converted; inspect replacement characters or convert the source to UTF-8 first.
not foundCheck spelling and root-relative location, then create or select an existing path.
outside the scan rootThe resolved target is outside root; select an appropriate root or keep external content excluded.
excluded because it is the current output fileThe path is the active -o/default output; choose another output if this is intentionally an input file.
not a content file (directory or special path)Directories do not have attached text; diagnose the file inside instead. Do not try to bundle devices or pipes.
disabled by --no-treeTree is disabled; use --no-tree=false if you want the map restored.
blocked by blacklistRead Rule to identify the built-in entry. Keep secrets out; bypass only for deliberately reviewed inputs.
blocked by ignore filtersInspect project/parent ignore rules, or use --no-ignore for a deliberate one-off.
blocked by excludeRemove or narrow the reported exclude. Adding include cannot beat exclude.
not included by includeBroaden the reported include, add a comma pattern, or clear it with an empty string.
skipped by max-sizeCompare Rule actual bytes with the KiB limit; raise -m only if the content budget permits.
skipped because binary fileA NUL byte was found. Omit binary content or export text from its original tool.
skipped because unreadableRead Rule’s metadata/read error; check access rights, file existence and broken links, then retry.

sections.title: Accepted options and diagnostic limits
sections.html:
One or more paths are required; relative paths resolve against the scan root, absolute paths are allowed. Root is the top-level PATH before explain. After explain, all profile options plus -p/--profile, --no-config and compatibility flags --dry-run, --save, --replace, -c/--copy, --show-arg are accepted. Options after explain override top-level options. --desc and the compatibility action flags do not save, replace, copy, generate a bundle or print resolved arguments; explain returns before normal execution. It may read and inspect files.

explain inspects the current filesystem; it can read content and traverse ignore rules. Missing paths have a Content result only. Resolve/permission errors can stop the diagnostic. Symlink canonicalization and ignore traversal may differ from a full scan, and files can change between runs; use dry-run as your final selection check. Diagnostics accept action flags for compatibility, but explain --save --copy --replace performs none of those actions.

output.title: Output and statistics
output.description: Choose an output path or clipboard, inspect a bundle, and interpret file counts and token estimates.

sections.title: Choose a delivery method
sections.html:
Use file output when you want to inspect, archive or share a reproducible artifact. Use clipboard output when you will paste immediately. Preview first in either case. This page uses a new demo folder so output paths and file counts are predictable:

In a new folder named demo, create the following files with a text editor. The text after each filename is its content; use a line break for each ↵. Use sample values only. Open a terminal in demo. Do not reuse a folder containing an existing .onesourcerc.

  • Cargo.toml: [package] ↵ name = "demo" ↵ version = "0.1.0" ↵ edition = "2021"
  • README.md: # Demo
  • src/main.rs: fn main() {}

OneSource must already be available as onesource. If it is not, follow Installation. All commands on this page start in this folder unless a step explicitly says otherwise.

sections.title: 1. Choose and verify the output path
sections.html:
Inside demo, preview a specifically named bundle:

onesource --no-config -o review.onesource --dry-run

Expect the planned path to end in demo/review.onesource and three processed files. No bundle is written. Remove dry-run to create that exact path:

onesource --no-config -o review.onesource

Confirm Output saved to: and open review.onesource in your editor. Omitting -o would use demo.onesource in the working directory. The output location does not automatically follow the scan root. To see this, move to demo’s parent and explicitly place the result inside demo:

cd ..
onesource demo --no-config -o demo/review.onesource --dry-run

Here the positional demo selects the scan root; -o is relative to the parent working directory. The existing review.onesource is excluded as the current output. Without -o, default demo.onesource would be written in the parent. Return before continuing:

cd demo

For a separate output folder, create it before bundling:

mkdir bundles
onesource --no-config -i "src/**" -o bundles/source.onesource

Expect one file block in bundles/source.onesource. OneSource does not create output parent directories. The extension is your choice; it does not select a different format. Repeating file output replaces the chosen existing file after successful rendering, without a confirmation prompt. A failed render preserves the previous output, but a configuration saved before scanning is not rolled back.

Default: canonical scan-root folder name plus .onesource (fallback project.onesource), written in the working directory. -o overrides it; no extension is enforced. Parent directories are not created. The current output is excluded even when blacklist is disabled. File mode renders into a unique temporary file beside output, flushes and syncs it, then replaces output. Render failure preserves previous output. On Windows replacement temporarily renames existing output to a backup and attempts restoration if rename fails. Config saves are separate and not rolled back.

sections.title: 2. Read the bundle rather than terminal progress
sections.html:
Open review.onesource from the previous step. First locate the project tree, then search for file paths. Here is the source block you should find; the rest of the bundle includes Cargo.toml and README.md:

<file path="src/main.rs">
fn main() {}
</file>

The path is relative to the scan root, making it easy to find the original file. The text between the tags is the attached content. Review that content before sharing. stdout contains the tree, progress and counts, not the full bundle; redirecting stdout does not replace opening the generated file.

my-project/
└── src/
    └── main.rs
<file path="src/main.rs">
fn main() {}
</file>

UTF-8 text, with optional tree followed by file blocks using relative paths. Path attributes escape &, <, >, quotes and apostrophes. File contents are inserted verbatim except lossy UTF-8 conversion; closing tags in contents are not escaped. This is a text convention, not a guaranteed valid XML document. Existing trailing newlines are kept and another newline is added before the closing tag.

sections.title: 3. Copy intentionally and understand dry-run/save
sections.html:
To paste source directly, preview a source-only selection, then copy it:

onesource --no-config -i "src/**" --dry-run

Expect only src/main.rs. Now send the same bundle to the clipboard:

onesource --no-config -i "src/**" --copy

Expect Output copied to clipboard successfully!. Paste into a text editor and verify the file block. No output file is created or updated. --copy requires a working desktop clipboard; if unavailable, use -o source.onesource instead.

If dry-run and copy are both present, preview wins:

onesource --no-config -i "src/**" --dry-run --copy

Expect NO COPY WAS MADE WHILE DRY RUN; the clipboard remains untouched. Saving configuration is different:

onesource --no-config -i "src/**" --dry-run --save

This creates or merges default in .onesourcerc even though no bundle is written. Open that config to confirm include="src/**". dry-run suppresses bundle and clipboard output, not --save. Use previews without --save while experimenting. For all four combinations, -o still determines the current-output exclusion, even if no file is written.

Copy mode buffers the complete output in memory. For large bundles prefer file mode; reduce selection before copying. The Profiles tutorial explains which settings --save preserves.

sections.title: 4. Interpret counts and tune a content budget
sections.html:
Run a full preview in the original demo root:

onesource --no-config --dry-run
Files Processed: 3
Files Skipped: 0
Estimated Output Tokens: ...

Generated .onesource files and .onesourcerc are blacklisted, so they do not inflate this count. Processed means attached files, not tree entries. Skipped zero does not mean nothing was filtered out: glob/ignore/blacklist exclusions are not counted there. Numbers shown as ... here are variable, not literal output.

For a recipient with limited context, first reduce files with include/exclude, then rerun the preview and compare estimated output tokens. -m limits each file, not total tokens. For example:

onesource --no-config -i "src/**" -m 1 --dry-run

The sample main.rs is below 1024 bytes, so it remains included. A file of exactly 1024 bytes is allowed; 1025 bytes is skipped. To investigate a size skip, run explain with the same -m and read the actual-byte Rule.

Files Processed counts successfully read attached files. Files Skipped counts inspection failures plus content/tree walk errors; it is not the number excluded by glob, ignore or blacklist and may count traversal errors from both walks. Per-file messages report content tokens only. Estimated Output Tokens uses cl100k_base on separately written tree, opening tag, content and closing fragments; it includes wrappers but can differ from tokenizing the final concatenated text and from your model tokenizer. Dry-run uses the same rendering estimate. No exact context-limit guarantee is provided.

update.title: Updating and source builds
update.description: Identify your installation, choose self-update or rebuilding, verify the result and recover from failures.

sections.title: 1. Identify the executable and choose an update route
sections.html:
Use this page when you already have OneSource installed and want a newer version. No demo project is required: updating acts on the executable, not the current project. First record the installed version:

onesource --version

A line such as onesource 3.5.1 identifies the binary version; this number is illustrative, not a claim about the latest release. Identify which installation your shell finds. On macOS/Linux:

command -v onesource

On Windows PowerShell:

Get-Command onesource

Check the returned path. If it is a compatible prebuilt binary, follow self-update below. If installed with Cargo or built for a custom platform, use the Cargo/source steps. Multiple installations can make a successful update appear ineffective if PATH later picks another binary. Read Installation if no executable is found.

sections.title: 2. Update a compatible prebuilt binary
sections.html:
You need internet access to GitHub, a supported release asset and write access to the executable’s directory. Run the update command without a project path or profile options:

onesource update

Read the printed Target, Current version and Latest version. If it says Already up to date., it did not download or replace anything. Otherwise it downloads beside the executable. On Unix, expect an Updated onesource message; on Windows it launches replacement after the process exits. Open a new terminal before checking:

onesource --version

Compare this with the Latest version that the update printed and verify the selected executable path again. The project and .onesourcerc are not part of the update. If permission or network errors occurred, do not treat a download message alone as completion; follow recovery below.

Current version comparison strips v/V and prerelease suffixes and compares numeric dot components; nonnumeric versions fall back to normalized inequality. This is not complete SemVer ordering. The command uses GitHub’s latest-release metadata, not a user-selected version.

sections.title: 3. Update Cargo installs or rebuild source
sections.html:
For a Cargo installation, keep your platform’s native build by rebuilding the crate. You need Rust, Cargo, a linker and network access to obtain dependencies:

cargo install onesource --force

Expect Cargo to finish installation, then verify onesource --version and the command path. Cargo normally installs to ~/.cargo/bin (Windows: %USERPROFILE%\.cargo\bin), or CARGO_HOME/bin when customized. If an older system binary takes priority, fix PATH or invoke the newly installed executable directly.

For a fresh source build, clone into a new directory, then build:

git clone https://github.com/TW-RF54732/onesource.git
cd onesource
cargo build --release

After Cargo finishes successfully, verify the built artifact directly on macOS/Linux:

./target/release/onesource --version

On Windows PowerShell use:

.\target\release\onesource.exe --version

Building does not install the result onto PATH. You can run this path directly or copy the binary to the intended executable location and verify that location. For an existing source checkout, obtain the desired source revision while preserving your own changes, then rebuild. Self-update would replace a Cargo/source binary with a published prebuilt asset; use rebuilding when custom architecture or build settings must be preserved.

sections.title: 4. Recover from an unsuccessful update
sections.html:
Work from the actual error, not repeated retries. For a permission failure, inspect Target and choose a writable installation location; reinstall a portable binary there or use Cargo. For network/API-limit or missing-asset errors, open manual download instructions and select the matching asset from GitHub Releases. After replacing or reinstalling, verify the direct path and --version before relying on PATH.

Published assets are Windows x86_64 onesource.exe, Linux x86_64 GNU onesource-linux, macOS Intel onesource-macos and Apple Silicon onesource-macos-arm64. Linux/Windows self-update selection does not check architecture, so other architectures should rebuild. Unsupported OS or macOS architecture fails. Unix requires sh, curl, grep, cut, head and chmod; Windows uses PowerShell. No checksum verification or transactional rollback is implemented. A failed update may leave onesource-update-PID next to the binary: ensure no update is still running before removing an identified leftover. The Unix installer’s completion banner alone is not verification; always run --version.

troubleshooting.title: Troubleshooting and limits
troubleshooting.description: Follow checks, corrections and verification for installation, missing files, config migration and output errors.

sections.title: Collect the symptom and current settings
sections.html:
This page starts from your own project, not a prepared demo. Preserve the failing command and its full error. Confirm whether the problem is finding OneSource, selecting files, loading config, writing output or copying. Use the relevant section below; changing unrelated flags can hide the real cause. For a bundling issue, record the scan root and working directory, then run the same command with --dry-run --show-arg and without --save/--replace/--copy.

onesource --dry-run --show-arg

This uses your existing profile/default; append your original include/exclude/-p options when reproducing the problem. show-arg prints resolved settings after preview. If loading config itself fails, there will be no resolved settings; use the migration section. Preview still reads files, so inaccessible inputs can produce warnings.

sections.title: Command not found, wrong version or permission denied
sections.html:
Check which executable is selected

On macOS/Linux:

command -v onesource
onesource --version

On Windows PowerShell:

Get-Command onesource
onesource --version

If no path is found, reopen the terminal after installation, then confirm the installation folder is on PATH. Portable executables can be run directly with ./onesource or .\onesource.exe from their folder. If a path is found but the version is unexpected, compare it with the binary you installed; correct PATH or invoke the intended path directly and verify again.

Check the kind of permission error

A manually downloaded Unix executable may need chmod +x onesource in its folder. Installation to /usr/local/bin may require sudo; use a writable user directory or Cargo if you cannot modify it. A bundling write error concerns the output parent, not executable permission: choose an existing writable output folder. For download failures, check GitHub/network/API limits and use the platform-specific release asset. After any reinstall, verify --version; the Unix installer does not fail fast on every command, so its completion banner is insufficient.

sections.title: A file is missing or a warning appears
sections.html:
Choose one missing relative path, then explain it with the same profile and filters as your failing run. Replace the example path and options with yours:

onesource explain src/main.rs -i "src/**"

Read Content Result and Rule. blocked by exclude requires narrowing exclude, not adding include. not included by include requires broadening include. blocked by ignore filters requires reviewing .gitignore/.ignore or a deliberate --no-ignore. blocked by blacklist requires inspecting the built-in Rule; keep real secrets excluded. A saved profile can supply any of these rules, so do not add --no-config to a diagnostic if the original command loaded configuration.

For size warnings, preserve the same limit:

onesource explain src/main.rs -m 1

Read actual bytes in Rule; 1 KiB allows up to 1024 bytes. A NUL byte makes content binary; export text or leave it out rather than changing size. For unreadable results, inspect the metadata/read error, check access rights and broken links, then retry. Non-UTF-8 text is included with replacement characters: convert to UTF-8 first if exact text matters. Re-run the original preview after the correction, then inspect the saved bundle.

If a path is shown in Tree but not Content, they may have separate filters, or content may fail size/read/binary checks. Directory symlinks are not recursively followed; outside-root file symlinks are skipped. Non-UTF-8 filenames display lossily, so different names can look identical. Read the diagnostic walkthrough for a complete worked example.

sections.title: Config fails to load: back up and migrate
sections.html:
If an error mentions an incompatible old format, open scan-root/.onesourcerc and make a backup copy outside the project before editing. A flat option object is the old shape:

{
  "include": "src/**",
  "max_size": 100,
  "no_tree": true
}

Keep the same option values, but wrap them in a named profile. To preserve unnamed-run behavior, name it default:

{
  "profiles": {
    "default": {
      "include": "src/**",
      "max_size": 100,
      "no_tree": true
    }
  }
}

Save valid JSON, with strings quoted, true/false unquoted, max_size numeric and no trailing commas. Now validate before saving other settings:

onesource profile show default --json

Expect the inner object with the same three fields. Then verify the resulting selection:

onesource --dry-run

Expect the default profile loaded and no tree. Files depend on your project’s src directory. If normal bundling must continue while you repair config, onesource --no-config --dry-run bypasses loading without modifying it. It does not repair it.

Invalid JSON or field types still require manual correction. Unknown fields may be ignored and then lost when rewritten. --no-config does not bypass management reads or --save reads; do not try to overwrite broken config through --save. For a missing named profile, check list or create it; for --replace without --save, either add --save intentionally or remove --replace. Avoid simultaneous config edits, since writes are not atomic.

sections.title: Output directory or clipboard fails
sections.html:
For Output directory does not exist, remember that -o is relative to the current working directory, even if the scan root is elsewhere. Create the output folder first. From your project root, using a new folder name:

mkdir bundles
onesource -o bundles/review.onesource --dry-run

Check the planned path, then run without dry-run. If permissions fail, select another existing writable folder. A previous output is preserved on render failure, but --save may already have changed configuration.

For clipboard initialization/flush failures, avoid --copy in remote or headless environments. Produce a file instead:

onesource -o review.onesource

Expect Output saved to and inspect the text with an editor. If you previously included --dry-run --copy, no copy was attempted; remove dry-run only when the preview is correct and a clipboard is available. A stale clipboard can otherwise look like successful output.

sections.title: Limits to account for after the fix
sections.html:
Selection and reading are separate steps; concurrent changes can affect output. Files are read whole; copy mode also buffers the complete bundle. Dry-run still reads and tokenizes. Token estimates are approximate. The blacklist is a fixed safeguard, not a complete secret detector. Output overwrites the chosen file after successful rendering; there is no confirmation prompt. Parent folders must exist. Normal output is a file or clipboard, not a stdout-only mode. There is no configuration inheritance, profile export command or recursive config discovery.

After resolving an issue, repeat the original preview, inspect the intended output and confirm the selected executable/config path. To recover from self-update failure use Updating; it has a different failure path from bundling.
